## Summary

Adds an opt-in BF16 unquantized linear fast path that wraps CUDA BF16 `F.linear` calls in a per-shape `torch.compile(..., mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs")` kernel.

The path is disabled by default and enabled with:

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_UNQUANT_BF16_LINEAR_TORCH_COMPILE=1
```
Key changes:

- Add VLLM_ENABLE_UNQUANT_BF16_LINEAR_TORCH_COMPILE
- Route eligible CUDA BF16 unquantized linears through a local torch.compile wrapper
- Cache compiled kernels by exact tensor shape/stride/dtype/device
- Avoid compiling during CUDA graph capture; only reuse previously warmed shapes
- Patch relevant Inductor/Dynamo autotune and cache knobs lazily when the path is first used
- Add focused dispatch, predicate, cache, fallback, and config tests

author: bpamiri
body:
## Summary

Closes finding #9 in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-29-fresh-vm-onboarding-findings.md` (introduced by batch A in PR #2359).

A first-time user following Wheels guides chapter 6b — *"The Built-in Way"* — found that `wheels.auth.SessionStrategy` couldn't be wired up. Login succeeded, the session struct populated, but every subsequent protected request failed with `No authentication strategy supports this request` and redirected to `/login`. The chapter is unfollowable as written.

Root cause: `Injector.cfc:asSingleton()` walked `variables.mappings` via for-in to find the just-mapped key. Lucee's HashMap-backed struct switches to hash-bucket iteration order once enough keys are registered to span multiple buckets — and the framework's `wheels.Bindings` registers ~20 mappings before user code runs. So when `services.cfm` called `injector().map("authenticator").to("wheels.auth.Authenticator").asSingleton()`, the iteration ended on `global` (the framework's first-registered binding), and `singletonFlags["global"] = true` was set instead of `singletonFlags["authenticator"]`. `service("authenticator")` then returned a fresh component on every call — and the strategy registered on it in `onApplicationStart` was silently lost on the next request.

The existing `InjectorSpec` test that asserted singleton caching was correct but only registered 1 mapping, putting all keys in the same hash bucket, where iteration happens to match insertion order. Real apps hit the bug at scale.

## Changes

### Framework
- **`vendor/wheels/Injector.cfc`** — Track `variables.lastMappedName` explicitly in `to()`. Have `asSingleton()` and `asRequestScoped()` consult that slot instead of iterating `variables.mappings`. Delete the now-unused `$findLastMappingKey()` helper.
- **`vendor/wheels/auth/Authenticator.cfc`** — Distinguish "no strategies registered" (now a diagnostic error pointing at the wiring) from "strategies registered but none claim this request" (existing generic message). The previous collapsed messages cost the original user ~30 minutes of wrong-trail debugging.

### Tests
- **`vendor/wheels/tests/specs/di/InjectorLifecycleSpec.cfc`** — New spec. Reproduces the bug at scale (20+ mappings) plus simpler cases. Without the fix: 2 of 4 cases fail. With the fix: 4/4 pass.
- **`vendor/wheels/tests/specs/di/InjectorSpec.cfc`** — Smoke test using the real `wheels.Bindings` (not the empty `TestBindings`) so the test exercises the same key-count regime the bug surfaces under.
- **`vendor/wheels/tests/specs/auth/AuthenticatorSpec.cfc`** — Updated existing zero-strategies test to assert the new diagnostic. Pinned the registered-but-none-claim case with the original message.
- **`vendor/wheels/tests/specs/auth/AuthMiddlewareSpec.cfc`** — Updated the parallel zero-strategies test in the middleware path.

### Docs
- **`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-29-fresh-vm-batch-d-di-singleton.md`** — Plan that drove this work (committed up-front for traceability).

## Test plan

- [x] `tools/test-local.sh di` passes 5/5 consecutive runs (3347 → 3351 tests, 0 fail, 0 error)
- [x] Full local suite stable (`tools/test-local.sh` no filter): **3351 pass, 0 fail, 0 error** in ~21s on Lucee 7 + SQLite
- [x] Hypothesis ruled out: `$findLastMappingKey` returns the wrong key only at scale (verified via instrumented full-app reproduction); 1-3-mapping unit tests pass even pre-fix
- [ ] Cross-engine matrix in CI (Adobe CF, Lucee 5/6/7, multiple databases)
- [ ] Manual: scaffold a fresh app, follow [chapter 6b](https://guides.wheels.dev/v4-0-0-snapshot/start-here/tutorial/06-authentication/) verbatim, confirm session login + logout work end-to-end

## Coordination with batch A

The triage doc this finding lives in (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-29-fresh-vm-onboarding-findings.md`) was introduced by [PR #2359 batch A](https://github.com/wheels-dev/wheels/pull/2359) and isn't on `develop` yet. Once both PRs merge, a follow-up commit on `develop` will mark finding #9 as shipped in the triage's "Shipped" table with the SHAs from this PR.

## Pourquoi

Quand l'utilisateur lance un Quick Voice Call sur YouTube **depuis l'extension Chrome** (path V1 = `video_id`), aucune ligne `Summary` n'était créée immédiatement. La vidéo n'apparaissait donc PAS dans l'historique web / mobile / extension tant que l'auto-analyse Mistral n'avait pas encore terminé d'écrire `full_digest` — soit plusieurs secondes à plusieurs minutes plus tard.

À l'inverse, le path V3 mobile (`video_url`) crée déjà un placeholder `Summary` au début de la session pour permettre au client de deep-link sur `/analysis/[id]` immédiatement (cf. lignes 1247-1274 du router avant ce PR).

Ce PR aligne le path V1 sur le comportement V3 → **un seul historique cohérent sur les 3 plateformes**.

## Ce qui change

### `backend/src/voice/router.py` (+55 lignes)

Dans `create_voice_session`, après la branche V3 placeholder et avant la création de la `VoiceSession` :

- Si `request.is_streaming + request.video_id + pas v3_url_path` :
  - On vérifie qu'aucun `Summary` n'existe déjà pour `(video_id, user_id)` via un `SELECT ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1`.
  - Si aucun → on crée un placeholder `Summary` avec :
    - `user_id`, `video_id`
    - `video_title = request.video_title or f"[En cours] YT {video_id}"`
    - `video_url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}"`
    - `platform = "youtube"`, `mode = "standard"`, `lang = request.language or "fr"`
  - `db.add` + `commit` + `refresh`
- La `VoiceSession.summary_id` est calculée en cascade : `v3_summary.id ?? v1_summary.id ?? request.summary_id`.

### `backend/tests/voice/test_voice_session_v1_auto_analysis.py` (+88 lignes)

- Nouveau test `test_v1_cache_miss_plan_pro_creates_summary_placeholder` qui vérifie :
  - Exactement **1** `Summary` row ajouté.
  - `placeholder.video_id == "dQw4w9WgXcQ"`, `mode == "standard"`, `platform == "youtube"`, `video_url == "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"`, `lang == "fr"`.
  - La `VoiceSession.summary_id` pointe sur le placeholder.
- Le helper `_configure_db_for_cache` accepte un paramètre optionnel `captured: list` pour récupérer les rows passés à `db.add`.
- Docstring du helper mise à jour pour refléter les **deux** db.execute désormais (existing-summary check + cache check).

## Tests

Toute la suite voice reste verte :

```
backend/tests/voice/test_voice_session_v1_auto_analysis.py   ........  4/4
backend/tests/voice/test_voice_session_video_url.py          ........  5/5
backend/tests/voice/                                         ........ 144/144
```

En particulier :
- `test_voice_session_video_url.py::test_valid_youtube_url_creates_summary_and_session` (path V3, ne crée toujours qu'**1** Summary) reste green grâce au garde `not v3_url_path`.
- Les 3 tests V1 préexistants (`test_v1_cache_*`) restent green parce que le mock `mock_db_session.execute` retourne le même résultat pour les deux appels — sémantique cohérente avec la prod.

## Hors scope

- Pas de migration DB (le placeholder utilise les colonnes Summary existantes).
- Pas de touche au front extension (le `summary_id` était déjà retourné dans `VoiceSessionResponse`).
- Pas de gestion de la collision `(video_id, user_id)` au-delà du `LIMIT 1` (l'utilisateur qui re-clic sur la même vidéo n'aura pas de doublon).

## Summary
Pivot architectural sur l'identité utilisateur et le partage entre exploitations.

### Login fédéré
- **Login = email + mot de passe seuls**
- Si plusieurs Users ont le même couple (cas comptable / conseiller partagé entre exploitations), tous les tenants matchant deviennent accessibles via le tenant switcher **sans nouveau login**
- Le numéro d'exploitant (= code Exploitation, format `VD-1234567`) reste l'identifiant **partagé pour les invitations partenaires** (M16). Il n'est plus utilisé à la connexion.
- Le numéro est éditable par l'owner via `PATCH /tenants/me`

### Recadrage du switcher
Avant cette PR, on pouvait basculer la session entre son tenant home **et** les tenants des partenaires actifs. C'était une mauvaise piste — un partenariat ne donne pas accès à toute la base du client (pas son cheptel, pas son historique). Le switcher ne liste désormais que les **comptes fédérés** (même email+password). La saisie d'intervention chez un partenaire passera par un sélecteur "Pour qui ?" dans une PR Prestations à venir.

## Backend
- Schema `User` : `@@unique([email, tenantId])` au lieu de `email @unique` (un même email peut désigner plusieurs comptes, un par tenant)
- **Migration** `users_email_per_tenant` : drop unique simple, recréation
- `JwtPayload` : ajout `tenantIds[]` (liste des tenants fédérés)
- `AuthService.login()` : `findMany` + `bcrypt.compare` contre chaque User candidat ; le JWT retient `tenantIds` des matches
- `JwtAuthGuard` : `X-Active-Tenant-Id` validé contre `tenantIds` (compte fédéré) au lieu de `PartnerLink`
- `TenantsController` + Service :
  - `GET /tenants/accessible` lit `tenantIds` du JWT
  - `PATCH /tenants/me` édite numéro d'exploitant + nom + UFAM + BDTA
- DTO `UpdateTenantDto` avec regex `{canton}-{num}` ex `VD-1234567`
- Regex M16 `PartnerLink` assouplie pour accepter `VD-1234567` **et** l'ancien `AQ-...` (rétro-compat)

## Frontend
- Retire `PartnerTenantBanner` du shell
- `TenantSwitcher` : minimal si un seul tenant, dropdown sinon, icône Home uniquement (plus d'icône Handshake)
- Type `AccessibleTenant` : `kind: 'home'` uniquement

## Migration prod
Les codes existants (admin/demo/marie) sont **conservés tels quels** par la migration SQL — pas de réécriture automatique. L'owner pourra les passer au format UFAM (`VD-1234567`) via la nouvelle UI à venir.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm lint` ✓
- [x] `pnpm test` ✓ (104 tests)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` ✓
- [x] `pnpm build` ✓
- [ ] Vercel preview : login `demo@demo.ch / demo` → vérifier qu'on accède toujours
- [ ] Tester un compte fédéré : créer 2 Users avec même email/password sur 2 tenants → vérifier que le switcher liste les 2

## Suite (PRs à venir)
- **PR Prestations** : modèle Prestation + saisie d'intervention chez un partenaire avec sélecteur "Pour qui ?" + propagation auto
- **PR Mon exploitation (UI)** : page `/exploitation` pour éditer le numéro UFAM côté UI

## Summary

- `FPNegBehavior::FlipSignBit` cannot be reliably enforced on Bitwuzla, CVC5, or Z3's native FP support: all NaNs are a single equivalence class, so the resulting NaN's bit pattern is not guaranteed to match a literal sign-bit flip of the input bits.
- A `mkBVToIEEEFP` / `mkIEEEFPToBV` round-trip does not preserve NaN payloads either (verified with a probe — bitwuzla, z3, and cvc5 each return SAT for the disequality between input and round-tripped NaN bits), so it cannot rescue the behavior.
- Documentation-only change: docstring on `SMTSolver::mkFPNeg` in `src/camada.h` and the corresponding bullet in `README.md`. No behavioral change.

## Summary
Three small performance fixes in one PR:

- **#3377** — `crates/librefang-api/src/server.rs:1356,1366`: the 30s config hot-reload poller called `std::fs::metadata` from inside `tokio::spawn`. On a slow filesystem (NFS, sleeping disk) this blocked a tokio worker for the full duration of `stat()`; under a single-thread runtime it stalled every other task on each tick. Switched to `tokio::fs::metadata` via a small `read_mtime` helper preserving the original swallow-all-errors semantics.

- **#3768** — `crates/librefang-api/dashboard/vite.config.ts`: McpServersPage already migrated off `lucide-react/dynamic` to `lazy()` + named imports (#3945), but the dead path was still listed in `SINGLETON_DEPS`, so Vite pre-bundled the full ~1500-icon registry into the shared chunk regardless. Removed the entry and isolated `lucide-react` into its own `icons` manualChunk so adding a single icon to one route no longer bloats first-load on every other page.

- **#3668** — `crates/librefang-api/src/rate_limiter.rs`: the GCRA sweep was wired up in #3957 (calls `retain_recent()` every 5 minutes from the API GC task in `server.rs:1545-1552`). Added a regression test `test_retain_recent_evicts_idle_entry` that locks the `KeyedRateLimiter::len()` / `retain_recent()` contract the sweep depends on, so a future refactor cannot silently revert unbounded DashMap growth.

Closes #3668
Closes #3377
Closes #3768

## Test plan
- [ ] CI: `cargo test -p librefang-api` covers the new `test_retain_recent_evicts_idle_entry` regression.
- [ ] CI: `cargo build --workspace` confirms the `tokio::fs::metadata` swap compiles (no new error type to thread; `read_mtime` returns the same `Option<SystemTime>`).
- [ ] Manual: bundle-analyze the dashboard build and verify `lucide-react` is now in its own `icons` chunk and the `lucide-react/dynamic` dead path is gone.

author: erik-kroon
body:
This PR improves scanner performance and responsiveness by bounding serialized directory children, summarizing generated dependency/cache folders by default, adding exact deep-scan support, caching reusable package aggregates, and exposing progress bytes plus skip diagnostics through the scanner contract.

The previous scan path could spend too much time and memory traversing large generated trees and serializing enormous child lists, which made home-folder and dependency-heavy scans slow or hard to use; the root cause was that every directory was recursively materialized into the report without policy-aware summarization or bounded presentation output.

The fix splits native reporting into policy, JSON, summary, aggregate-cache, and scanner modules; adds CLI/UI exclude and deep-scan controls; shares scan lifecycle handling through a runtime abstraction; and packages the compiled scanner executable into the desktop app so packaged builds do not rely on a source checkout.

Validation: `bun --filter @zpace/scanner test`, `bun --filter web test --run`, `cd packages/scanner && bun run check-types`, `cd apps/desktop && bun run check-types`, `cd apps/web && bun run build`, `bun --filter desktop build:stable`, app-bundle inspection for `Resources/app/scanner/zpace-scanner`, and a manual executable-path scan with a missing source root.

body:
## Summary

Closes F-35 from the 2026-04-29 audit (cross-cutting theme B "input boundary validation"). F-29 already closed the f64 NaN/Inf side; this PR closes the size-bound side. Three new constants bound \`search\` query length and \`compute_match_spans\` input dimensions so abuse cases stop being O(N×M) on the server.

## Constants

| Name | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| \`SEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BYTES\` | 1024 (1 KiB) | Reject oversized queries early instead of letting embedder/FTS5 truncate silently. Predictable response shape, kills the upstream amplifier for the next two caps. |
| \`MATCH_SPAN_CONTENT_MAX_BYTES\` | 262144 (256 KiB) | Skip span computation on chunks larger than this. Typical heading-scoped chunks are a few KiB; cap is for malformed indexer state. \`compute_match_spans\` returns \`None\` (= "not computed"). |
| \`MATCH_SPAN_MAX_COUNT\` | 100 | Break out of the term scan once 100 spans are pushed. Dedup runs after, so the final count is \`<= 100\`. Prevents a 1-char query × long content from blowing up the JSON response size. |

These are intentionally constants, not config fields — they exist to bound abuse, not legitimate use. The chosen ceilings are well past where embedding/FTS5 stop being useful.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test\`: 331 pass / 0 fail (was 328, +3 new in \`server::tests\`)
  - \`test_compute_match_spans_oversize_content_returns_none\`
  - \`test_compute_match_spans_at_cap_content_succeeds\` (boundary)
  - \`test_compute_match_spans_count_capped\` (asserts \`<= MATCH_SPAN_MAX_COUNT\`)
- [x] \`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings\` clean
- [x] \`cargo fmt --check\` clean
- [x] Existing 6 \`compute_match_spans\` tests still pass (ASCII basic / case-insensitive / non-ASCII / utf-8 chunk / empty / no match)

## Behavior changes

- An MCP client that sends a query > 1024 bytes now gets:
  \`\`\`json
  { "error": "query is too large: 2048 bytes (max 1024 bytes). For long-form retrieval, slice the query or use multiple smaller calls." }
  \`\`\`
  Previously the query would flow through the embedder which truncates at its own internal limit (model-dependent). Predictable error is better.
- A chunk over 256 KiB returns no \`match_spans\` field (omitted via \`#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]\`). Previously that path was \`O(content_len)\` per term.
- Span count saturates at 100. Most queries already produced far fewer; a pathological 1-char query is the only case that changes.

## Notes

CHANGELOG entry under \`[Unreleased] / Security\`. README en+ja gain a short "Input bounds (defensive, v0.5.1+)" sentence in the Search section.

author: shuuri-labs
body:
## Describe your changes

Adds a standalone installer script (`release_files/install-steamos.sh`) for deploying NetBird on SteamOS/Bazzite as a user-level service optimized for game streaming.

SteamOS (or other SteamOS-like distros) uses an immutable A/B partition scheme with a read-only rootfs, which breaks traditional installation methods. This script takes a different approach from the `systemd-sysext` pattern (used by e.g. Tailscale) by keeping everything in `/home` and using Linux file capabilities instead of running as root:

- **User-level service** — runs as the `deck` user with `systemctl --user`, binary and config live under `/home`
- **Real kernel TUN interface** — uses userspace WireGuard (wireguard-go) with a kernel TUN device for proper network performance (important for Moonlight/Sunshine game streaming)
- **File capabilities instead of root** — `sudo setcap cap_net_admin,cap_net_raw+eip` grants the binary the network capabilities it needs without running as root (one-time sudo at install, reapplied per update)
- **No sysext / overlay** — no version pinning, no extension-release files to break on OS updates
- **Survives all OS updates** — nothing on the read-only rootfs
- **SHA-256 checksum verification** — validates downloads against the release checksums.txt before installing
- **Atomic updates** — downloads and verifies the new binary to a staging directory before stopping the running service, so failed downloads leave the existing installation untouched
- **Supports install, update, and uninstall** via `--update` and `--uninstall` flags
- **Auto-connect** with `NB_SETUP_KEY` environment variable for headless auth
- **`FORCE=true` escape hatch** for other immutable Linux distros (e.g. Bazzite)

### Why not netstack mode?

An earlier iteration used `NB_USE_NETSTACK_MODE=true` for a fully rootless install. However, netstack routes all traffic through a userspace gVisor network stack, which adds latency and jitter unsuitable for real-time game streaming. The TUN + file capabilities approach gives kernel-level routing performance while still keeping all files in `/home`.

body: ## Summary Tightens password-protected and capability-restricted enforcement across the public output paths that produce job listing data: AJAX, REST, RSS (custom and core), JSON-LD, the listing-card templates, and the Recent / Featured Jobs widgets. Previously these paths could surface listing data the visible templates already denied. ## Changes **`wp-job-manager-functions.php`** - `get_job_listings()` now adds `'has_password' => false` to its default `$query_args`, so password-protected listings are excluded at the WP_Query layer for every consumer. - The listings transient cache key now folds in viewer auth state (`'u' . get_current_user_id()` for logged-in users, `'anon'` otherwise) so cached payloads don't cross auth boundaries. - `get_job_listings_keyword_search()` no longer adds a duplicative `post_password = ''` SQL clause — the query-level `has_password=false` covers all viewers. **`includes/class-wp-job-manager-cache-helper.php`** - Adds option-event hooks (add/update/delete) on `job_manager_browse_job_listings_capability` and `job_manager_view_job_listing_capability` that bump the `get_job_listings` transient version, so cached listings don't outlive the policy that produced them. **`includes/class-wp-job-manager-post-types.php`** - `job_feed()` (custom RSS) gates on browse capability with an empty feed, and adds `has_password=false` to its query. - New `gate_feed_query_for_listings()` on `pre_get_posts` extends the same gate to every core feed slug scoped to `post_type=job_listing` (`?feed=rss2&post_type=job_listing`, `?feed=atom&post_type=job_listing`, etc.). Without this, anonymous viewers could see a password-protected listing's title, permalink, slug, and pubdate via the default RSS feed even with the browse-capability option configured. - `get_job_listing_fields()` default `auth_view_callback` swaps from `null` to a new `auth_check_can_view_job_listing` static method that returns false on password-protected or view-cap-denied listings; meta fields without an explicit override now flow through this gate. **`includes/class-wp-job-manager-rest-api.php`** - `prepare_job_listing()` blanks top-level fields (`title.rendered`, `link`, `slug`, `featured_media`) and removes the `wp:featuredmedia` link relation when the viewer can't unlock the listing or is denied by view capability. The `meta` block is emptied in the same path. - `exclude_filled_from_query()` short-circuits the REST collection (`post__in = [0]`) when browse capability denies the viewer, and adds `has_password=false` unconditionally. **`includes/class-wp-job-manager-ajax.php`** - `get_listings()` returns a success-shaped empty JSON payload when browse capability denies the viewer, matching what the JS client expects. **`includes/widgets/class-wp-job-manager-widget-recent-jobs.php`, `…-widget-featured-jobs.php`** - Both widgets now early-return from `widget()` ahead of `get_cached_widget()` when `job_manager_user_can_browse_job_listings()` denies the viewer. Without this, the widgets bypassed the browse-capability gate the AJAX / REST / RSS paths apply, and could be served from `WP_Widget`'s built-in cache after a policy change. **`wp-job-manager-template.php`** - `wpjm_output_job_listing_structured_data()` now also requires `job_manager_user_can_view_job_listing()`; the `wp_footer` JSON-LD emitter honors the same view-capability check the visible template applies. **`templates/content-*-job_listing.php`** - Adds a defense-in-depth password + view-capability gate at the top of each listing-card template so theme overrides can't bypass the per-post checks. **`tests/php/tests/security/`** (new + extended) - Test classes covering: keyword search + transient cache for password-protected listings, AJAX/REST/RSS/JSON-LD denial under browse / view capability configuration, REST single + collection behavior for password-protected listings (including verification that the `wp:featuredmedia` link relation is removed), and the new `pre_get_posts` feed gate (default feed excludes password-protected, browse-cap-denied feed short-circuits, non-job-listing feed queries are not affected). ## Manual test results Verified against `make up` / wp-env at `http://localhost:8888` with subscriber registration enabled: - Original PoC closed: subscriber AJAX `?jm-ajax=get_listings&search_keywords=ULTRAVIOLET` → `found_jobs=False`; all six oracle tokens (`ULTRAVIOLET`, `InsiderCo`, `MAGENTA`, `WAREHOUSE-7`, `ceo-secret`, `tagline`) return `ok`. - Custom `?feed=job_feed&search_keywords=ULTRAVIOLET` → 0 items. - Default `?feed=rss2&post_type=job_listing` → public listings present, password-protected listings absent. - REST single (`/wp/v2/job-listings/?_embed=1`) returns blanked title/link/slug/featured_media/meta and no `wp:featuredmedia` link relation. - REST collection excludes password-protected, includes public. - With `job_manager_browse_job_listings_capability=["read"]`: anonymous AJAX, REST collection, custom `job_feed`, default `rss2&post_type=job_listing`, and Recent Jobs widget all return empty / no output. Subscriber Alice (has `read`) still sees listings. - Cache amplification fixed: subscriber priming the cache for a keyword does not surface password-protected listings on a subsequent anonymous request (separate transient slots verified in `wp_options`). ## Known follow-ups - #2941 — REST `content.rendered` / `excerpt.rendered` are not blanked for view-capability-denied (non-password-protected) listings. Pre-existing on trunk; this PR closes most of the gap but leaves the body fields for a follow-up. ### Release Notes * Fixes a series of information disclosure issues affecting password-protected and capability-restricted job listings. ## Test plan - [x] `make lint` — clean - [x] `make test` — 463 tests, 1891 assertions, 3 skipped (geocode, same as baseline) - [x] Manual: REST single endpoint for a password-protected listing returns blanked title/link/slug/featured_media and empty meta; `?_embed=1` does not surface the attachment. - [x] Manual: with browse capability set, AJAX `get_listings`, REST collection, RSS `job_feed`, default `?feed=rss2&post_type=job_listing`, and Recent Jobs widget return empty payloads to denied viewers; JSON-LD does not emit on the single-listing footer. - [x] Manual: with no capability config (default), public listings still surface to anonymous viewers in AJAX / REST / RSS (custom and default) / JSON-LD / widgets, and the keyword search returns public listings. - [x] Manual: cached listings populated by an authenticated user do not surface to a subsequent anonymous request on the same query. ---- | Plugin build for cc2d8a0c66103cb1d74cf0572e4a25fbad7f2982 | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | 📦 [Download plugin zip](https://wpjobmanager.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/wp-job-manager-zip-2940-cc2d8a0c.zip) | | ▶️ [Open in playground](https://wpjobmanager.com/playground/?core=2026/05/2940-cc2d8a0c) |

author: thebenignhacker
body:
## Summary

Closes #137 (render half).

Pre-fix, `hackmyagent check <path> --nanomind` on a malicious skill produced output of the form:

```
HIGH  (low confidence — capped from CRITICAL)
This artifact is a security documentation (AST-CRED-001) documenting a
credential security vulnerability in an AST-CRED-001 file. The document
explicitly describes a credential harvesting attack pattern: a request
for "credentials" from ...
(run with --verbose for full analysis)
Confidence: low confidence | nanomind-analyst-v0.1.0 (3110ms)
```

Three problems landed at once:

1. **Circular check-ID-as-topic phrasing.** "is a security documentation (AST-CRED-001) documenting a credential security vulnerability in an AST-CRED-001 file" — the model mentioned the check ID twice as if it were a topic.
2. **Framed `SKILL.md` as documentation rather than the malicious artifact itself.** The malicious `exfil-skill/SKILL.md` IS the malicious artifact — frontmatter has `env:` with FAKE-shaped credentials, a `postRunHook: curl` exfil channel, and an OWASP LLM01 directive in the description. The summary read as if it were docs ABOUT a credential issue.
3. **Cap-from-CRITICAL stamp landed beside confident prose.** Users read the description and trusted it more than the dim parenthetical cap warning. "Model said critical, then HMA capped it" is the trust break we landed on ourselves.

## Render-layer fix

When `capAnalystThreatLevel(threatLevel, confidence)` reports `capped: true`, filter the threatAnalysis finding out of the renderable list at `src/cli.ts:1336-1352` (alongside the existing `isRenderableAnalystFinding` filter for low-confidence and low-severity). The static finding (e.g. `AST-CRED-001 Credential Harvesting Pattern`) still renders via its own path — the underlying threat is already represented; confidence-capped model output adds no actionable signal beyond it. The cap-from-CRITICAL stamp + the redundant `(low confidence — capped from CRITICAL)` suffix are gone.

## Out of scope (filed as follow-up)

The prompt template wording itself — bug (1) above — needs a NanoMind training/prompt change to drop check-ID-as-topic phrasing and to disambiguate "this artifact contains malicious patterns" vs "this artifact documents malicious patterns." That's a Wave-2 NanoMind-side item and lives in a separate issue.

## Phase 4.5 — Tier C (quick-pair only)

Pure render-layer change with no detection / scoring / heuristic effect. Per `feedback_phase45_tiered_protocol.md` tier table, Tier C → quick-pair only; full Phase 4.5 subagent not warranted. Quick-pair: malicious kitchen-sink + benign tiny-clean-repo both render unchanged in static-finding paths; the only difference is the suppressed `HIGH (low confidence — capped from CRITICAL)` analyst block.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run __tests__/cli/nanomind-summary-cap-filter.test.ts` — 7/7 pass
- [x] `npm test` — 1995/2021 pass (16 skipped, 10 todo)
- [x] `npm run release-smoke:corpus` — 12/12 fixtures pass
- [x] Quick-pair: malicious kitchen-sink + benign tiny-clean-repo render unchanged in their static-finding paths
- [x] Self-scan: `node dist/cli.js secure .` — `Security 89/100` (precedent waiver)

## Test contract pinned

`__tests__/cli/nanomind-summary-cap-filter.test.ts` (7 cases):
- `capAnalystThreatLevel` cap precondition: CRITICAL at 0.3 confidence → capped HIGH; CRITICAL at 0.9 doesn't cap; HIGH and below never cap
- Filter contract: drops capped threatAnalysis, keeps high-confidence threatAnalysis, keeps non-threatAnalysis tasks (intelReport / governanceReasoning / credentialContextClassification / checkExplanation) regardless of confidence, mixed-list ordering preserved

### Context

PR [#56489](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/56489) in PostHog/posthog added better error handling for unrepresentable decimal values when importing data from SQL sources. - The decimal precision limit (max precision 76, max scale 32)
- Three remediation options:
  - Constrain the column with a lower precision/scale
  - Cast it to text in a view
  - Round the values at the source
